chunks: "Everything whose meat is eaten—there is no harm in what comes out of it." As for what indicates the specification of chicken droppings:

(782) 69 — What the Shaykh, may Allah Most High support him, informed me of, from Abū al-Qāsim Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā and Aḥmad ibn Idrīs, from Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā, from Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from Fāris, who said:
A man wrote to him asking him about chicken droppings: is salat (prayer) permissible in it? So he wrote: "No."

key_terms.أُكِلَ لَحْمُهُ: an animal whose meat is lawful to eat
key_terms.تَخْصِيصِ: specification or exception to a general rule
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: there is no harm or objection

ai.seo_question: Is salat (prayer) valid if clothing is affected by chicken droppings?
ai.summary: This report discusses a legal ruling concerning impurity on clothing and the validity of salat (prayer). Although a general principle is mentioned regarding animals whose meat is eaten, this narration cites a specific report indicating an exception concerning chicken droppings, with the answer given: "No."
